Topic: Higher Order Derivatives: Understanding Rates of Change of Rates

Target audience: University students (Calculus I/II)

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite Review: The First Derivative

Lecture lines:
[Asset: curve_f] The first derivative f'(x) measures instantaneous slope.
[Asset: tangent_line] Think of this as velocity in a system.
[Asset: velocity_vector] It describes how the position changes over time.

Planned animations:
Fade in the function curve labeled f(x) in #FFFFFF.
Draw a tangent line at point a in #FF0000.
Animate the slope of the tangent line as f'(a).
Show the derivative graph f'(x) below the function.
Highlight the slope-derivative correspondence with a dashed line.

Section: section_2 — Defining the Second Derivative

Lecture lines:
[Asset: curve_f_prime] We derive the derivative again to get f''(x).
[Asset: slope_change] This is the rate of change of the rate.
[Asset: acceleration_vector] Effectively, it captures the system's acceleration.

Planned animations:
Display the function f'(x) in #FFFFFF.
Mark two points on f'(x) with different slopes.
Animate the rate of change of f'(x) as f''(x).

Section: section_3 — Higher Orders (n-th derivatives)

Lecture lines:
[Asset: curve_higher_order] Higher orders follow this same hierarchical pattern.
[Asset: jerk_label] The third derivative often represents sudden "jerk".
[Asset: n_th_derivative] It measures rapid change in acceleration.

Planned animations:
Display the sequence f'(x), f''(x), f'''(x).
Show the notation for f to the power of (n).
Animate the transition from derivative to derivative order.

Section: section_4 — Visualizing Curvature

Lecture lines:
[Asset: concave_up_down] The second derivative tells us about curvature.
[Asset: f_double_prime_pos] Positive values indicate concave-up graphs.
[Asset: f_double_prime_neg] Negative values mean the graph is concave-down.

Planned animations:
Show a concave up curve in #00FF00.
Show a concave down curve in #FF0000.
Label both curves with their concavity signs.

Section: section_5 — Summary & Synthesis

Lecture lines:
[Asset: hierarchy_table] We now have a full derivative hierarchy.
[Asset: dna_representation] These define the "DNA" of the motion.
[Asset: application_icons] Use this to predict behavior in complex systems.

Planned animations:
Review all derivative orders on screen in #FFFFFF.
Highlight the relationship between f, f', and f''.
Fade all labels to signify the conclusion.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: The First Derivative", [
            "The first derivative f'(x) measures instantaneous slope.",
            "Think of this as velocity in a system.",
            "It describes how the position changes over time."
        ])

        # Define axes and curve
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 5, 1], y_range=[-1, 3, 1], x_length=4, y_length=3)
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2 * x**3 - 0.5 * x**2 + 0.5, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "C6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(axes, curve)

        # Tangent line setup
        t = ValueTracker(1)
        tangent_line = always_redraw(lambda: TangentLine(curve, alpha=t.get_value(), length=2, color=RED))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.add(tangent_line)
        self.play(t.animate.set_value(3), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        # Visualizing derivative as slope
        slope_label = MathTex("f'(x)").set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(slope_label, "D3")
        self.play(Write(slope_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        # Show derivative curve
        deriv_curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.6 * x**2 - 1.0 * x, color="#00FF00")
        self.play(Create(deriv_curve))
        self.wait(1)

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])
